intro_html:
HB 1971 has not moved since it was referred to the House Energy Committee in October 2025, and the session ends on 30 November 2026, when bills that have not passed die. For the coming year, then, the rules in Philadelphia are PECO’s. Its interconnection page says applications “are required for all private generator facilities connecting to PECO’s distribution system”. An inverter-based unit of 10 kW or less, which includes an 800 W kit, goes through its Level 1 process under the Public Utility Commission’s interconnection rules, and PECO notes that contractors typically file the application for the customer.

Nor is there a statutory backstop for condo and townhouse owners: Pennsylvania has no law that stops a homeowners or condominium association from refusing solar. HB 1239, which passed the House 109–93 on 1 July 2026 and now sits in the Senate Urban Affairs and Housing Committee, would change that only for a “detached roof” solely owned by an individual. As written it would not reach a panel on a balcony railing in a multi-unit building, and it faces the same 30 November deadline. Renters need the landlord’s agreement in any case.

balco.nyc’s calculator models a specific Philadelphia address and lets you enter the rate from your own PECO bill in place of the state average.

faq: Does PECO require an application for a plug-in solar panel?

PECO’s interconnection page says applications are required for all private generator facilities connecting to its distribution system, and inverter-based units of 10 kW or less go through its Level 1 process. Pennsylvania has no plug-in solar law exempting small devices; HB 1971, which would, has not left committee.
Would Pennsylvania's HB 1239 let condo owners put solar on a balcony?

As written, no. HB 1239, which passed the House on 1 July 2026, bars condominium and planned-community associations from prohibiting solar only on a “detached roof” solely owned by an individual. It says nothing about balconies, and it is still in a Senate committee with the session ending on 30 November 2026.
